reason: On this page 'referral platform' is the generic name for any FHIR server an app connects to: the next sentence says the capability statements 'provide further specifications for servers', and the sections below connect apps to 'the referral source (Provider) or referral target (CBO) system' and to 'Provider or Coordination Platform system'. Narrowing the SHOULD to coordination platforms would drop referral source and referral target servers from its scope (normative force). Raise one glossary_feedback note for the page's 'referral platform' pattern instead.

Line 11 says this section covers connecting the app 'to the referral source (Provider) or referral target (CBO) system'. The platforms the app registers with are those systems, not (only) a coordination platform; the rewrite changes meaning.

Same sentence continues 'Alternatively, the patient might select the clinic/facility from a list' and the step is 'repeated for each referral source': the platform identified is the provider's (referral source's) server, not a coordination platform.

Generic 'referral platform' for the provider/CBO server the patient app connects to (section scope set at line 11). Calling it a coordination platform mislabels the referral source's system as the intermediary's.
Same clause as @1713: the FHIR API being accessed is the referral source (Provider) or referral target (CBO) server, not specifically a coordination platform.

Step 4 of the Patient/Client flow, which the page says is 'repeated for each referral source'. 'Referral platform' is the page's generic server term, not the glossary CP; the capitalisation inconsistency is in a non-glossary phrase and is not a Form finding for T-CP.

The examples in the same line are 'Epic, Unite US' and the section intro (line 28) names the target as 'the referral source (Provider or Coordination Platform system)'. 'Referral platforms' deliberately spans EHRs and CPs; 'coordination platforms' would exclude Epic.

Step 2 says the 'Referral Source provides CBO ... with a URL to the API'; the credentials come from that referral source, which per line 28 may be a Provider or a CP. Rewriting as coordination platform narrows the meaning.

Self-referral page; D-2 option B (recommended) allows 'person' here. The bullet defines the 'Individual/Patient' role, so 'A patient or an authorized representative ...' would define patient with patient, and the following sentence keeps 'The person is the subject of the referral'.

Same bullet as @2179: self-referral context under D-2 option B, and the 'person' here is deliberately the human being represented (the representative is not the patient). Changing only this clause also leaves the sentence mixing 'person' and 'patient'.

'Individual or entity' is the FHIR pairing for ServiceRequest.requester (Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Patient, RelatedPerson vs Organization/Device). The requester is often not the patient; 'the patient or entity asking for the service' would misstate the element.

Documentation for the QuestionnaireResponse 'author' search parameter. QuestionnaireResponse.author may be a Practitioner, RelatedPerson, Organization or Device as well as the Patient; 'particular patient' would misdescribe the parameter (the 'patient'/'subject' parameters cover that).
Same 'author' search-parameter text as @68797 in the server-mode rest block; the author is whoever filled in the response, not necessarily the patient.

The subject is 'systems that originate requests for service ... also recipients of requests', a parallel originate/receive pairing about systems. The glossary's referral target is an organizational actor and names no system actor (domain note), so 'systems ... may also be referral targets' would mislabel systems; the proposed phrase 'referral targets for requests for service' is also redundant.

'The recipient' refers back to the '[referral recipient] systems' and 'receivers' earlier in the sentence and is predicated with 'doesn't have local persistence or FHIR server capabilities', which is a system property. Its complement is the CapabilityStatement name ('light' Referral Recipient). The glossary names no system actor for the referral target; leave it.
